DECISION D35 - FROZEN N1B MEASUREMENT

News state
For each issuer and fold, count admissible novel exact-title clusters in a decision cycle, apply log1p, then map the value through the preceding eight-quarter TRAIN empirical distribution. High intensity requires a nonzero count and percentile at least 0.80.

Outcome
From the following session open, compute the square root of the sum of squared log moves across five sessions, then divide by the issuer's TRAIN median five-session path volatility.

Leakage controls
Outcome paths must end inside the same OOS quarter. ECDFs and volatility scales use TRAIN-complete rows only. FB and META are one issuer with point-in-time ticker validity.

Evidence
Mean fold Spearman correlation is 0.107321. All 12 OOS quarters have positive rank correlation between issuer-local news intensity and relative future path volatility. All 12 also have positive high-intensity-minus-other separation.

Meaning
The association is modest in rank magnitude but unusually stable across the frozen quarter sequence. Stability, not one pooled headline number, is the core evidence.

Boundary
Five-session outcomes overlap, so daily issuer observations are not independent hypothesis-test trials. No p-value, causal claim, or policy return is asserted.

DECISION D35 - LOCAL CALIBRATION IS ESSENTIAL

Evidence
In the 2024Q4 fold, the p80 raw-count threshold is 20 clusters for AAPL and 27 for TSLA, versus only one for CAT and KO. CAT and KO also have zero-news shares near 50 percent, while AAPL and TSLA have none.

Tie caveat
Counts are discrete. When many TRAIN days share the threshold count, the ECDF rule marks a broader state than a literal top 20 percent. Across OOS quarters, the high-state share ranges from 24.8 percent to 46.8 percent.

Meaning
The frozen gate tested a reproducible high-state definition; it did not prove that 0.80 is an optimal operational cutoff. Threshold search remains closed.
